builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ReQOR: Operator-Discrepancy Subspace Repair for Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors in Large Language Models
summary: Replaces security-guided quantization configuration selection and iterative gradient-based backdoor mitigation with a training-free repair: it measures per-module operator discrepancies between full-precision and quantized versions on identical states from the quantized trajectory, extracts dominant discrepancy directions on benign calibration data, and restores full-precision computation along those directions via a closed-form factorized residual adapter. Costs are a calibration pass over benign data plus, for full-span repair, extra memory to store the adapters; the low-rank variant reduces this overhead but may repair less completely. It can fail when the backdoor's discrepancy energy lies outside the identified dominant subspace, when calibration data do not activate the relevant directions, or against attacks whose mechanism does not manifest as local same-state operator discrepancies.
rationale: For a team that deploys quantized models obtained or fine-tuned from potentially untrusted sources, a training-free, calibration-only defense is cheap to validate, but the backdoor threat model is narrow enough that adoption should follow workload-specific testing.
technique: Operator-discrepancy subspace repair for quantized-model backdoors

claims.statement: Replaces security-guided quantization configuration selection and iterative gradient-based backdoor mitigation with a training-free repair: it measures per-module operator discrepancies between full-precision and quantized versions on identical states from the quantized trajectory, extracts dominant discrepancy directions on benign calibration data, and restores full-precision computation along those directions via a closed-form factorized residual adapter. Costs are a calibration pass over benign data plus, for full-span repair, extra memory to store the adapters; the low-rank variant reduces this overhead but may repair less completely. It can fail when the backdoor's discrepancy energy lies outside the identified dominant subspace, when calibration data do not activate the relevant directions, or against attacks whose mechanism does not manifest as local same-state operator discrepancies.

Substantial mitigation of quantization-conditioned backdoors while largely preserving benign utility across four LLMs, three PGD-based attacks, and three quantization formats; effective on a non-PGD outlier-injection attack where baselines largely fail. No multiplicative factor is reported in the abstract.
